site.components.closing.sub: It runs in the tab you already have open, on the machine you already have.
site.components.closing.title: Open a drawing in the next ten seconds.

site.content.audiences.architects.body: Open consultant DXFs, draw over them, and issue sheets at a real scale. Blocks with attributes turn doors and windows into schedules; layouts carry a GA and a detail sheet from one model.
site.content.audiences.architects.headli: Plans, sections and schedules without the seat licence.
site.content.audiences.architects.label: Architects
site.content.audiences.architects.point1: DXF round-trip with layers and blocks intact
site.content.audiences.builders.body: The editor is a standalone Angular component with a small API: hand it DXF text or a drawing id, receive the DXF back on save, and keep your own identity system. Run it on your origin or ours.
site.content.audiences.builders.headline: A drafting surface you can embed in your own product.
site.content.audiences.builders.label: Product teams
site.content.audiences.engineers.body: Dimension values, plot-scale overrides, per-style fonts and lineweights are imported faithfully, so a bridge general arrangement opens as issued. Measure, mark up and export without a conversion step.
site.content.audiences.engineers.headlin: GA drawings that read the way AutoCAD wrote them.
site.content.audiences.engineers.label: Civil & structural engineers
site.content.audiences.students.body: Nothing to install and nothing to license per seat. The command line, aliases and prompts match AutoCAD, so what students learn transfers, and the UI speaks fourteen languages.
site.content.audiences.students.headline: The same commands as the industry, on any laptop in the room.
site.content.audiences.students.label: Students & educators
site.content.audiences.students.point1: Free plan with the full toolset
site.content.audiences.students.point3: Works on Chromebooks and shared machines
site.content.audiences.teams.body: Organizations with owner, admin, member and viewer roles; shared folders; view or edit links you can email. Two people saving the same drawing get a clear choice instead of a silent overwrite.
site.content.audiences.teams.headline: One set of drawings, one place, with a version for every save.
site.content.audiences.teams.label: Studios & teams

Every action is validated, classed safe, review or destructive, previewed, and undoable. Bring your own model: a local Ollama server or an OpenRouter key.

Cloud drawings are versioned, conflicts are caught, and a save made offline is kept in the browser until you save again online.

site.content.principles.ai.body: The assistant compiles plain language into ordinary editor commands, validates them, labels the risk and shows you before it commits. Everything it does is undoable, and the audit log stays on your device.
site.content.principles.ai.title: AI proposes, you decide.
site.content.principles.browser.body: Parsing, rendering, snapping, hatching and plotting all run on your machine, in the tab. The server holds identity, files and versions. A large drawing does not need a large upload to draw a line.
site.content.principles.browser.title: The browser is enough.
site.content.principles.ownership.body: DXF export is on every plan, including Free. If you stop paying your drawings stay readable and exportable. There is no proprietary format standing between you and your work.
site.content.principles.ownership.title: Your files are yours.
site.content.principles.parity.body: A drawing must open in CADO the way it was issued: same dimension values, same text, same lineweights. When a DXF renders differently from AutoCAD we treat it as a bug and fix the importer, not the drawing.
site.content.principles.parity.title: AutoCAD parity is the bar, not a feature.
site.content.timeline.accounts.body: Sign in, save to your account, Recent, My Drawings with folders, Trash, safe concurrent saves, drag-and-drop upload.
site.content.timeline.accounts.title: 1.1 — accounts and cloud drawings
site.content.timeline.billing.body: The Free tier limits advertised on the pricing page are recorded today and will be enforced once billing goes live.
site.content.timeline.billing.title: Plan enforcement, billing live, team invoicing
site.content.timeline.editor.body: Lines, polylines, arcs, hatch, dimensions, blocks, layouts, DXF in and out, twelve themes.
site.content.timeline.editor.title: 1.0 — the editor
site.content.timeline.fidelity.body: Imported drawings render as AutoCAD renders them; layout tabs show the model and accept every tool; HiDPI-crisp canvases; the assistant understands which entities you mean.
site.content.timeline.fidelity.title: DXF fidelity and layouts
site.content.timeline.product.body: Feedback, notifications, personal info, plans and pricing, and a run of editor fixes.
site.content.timeline.product.title: 1.2 — a product around the editor
site.content.timeline.threeD.body: A phased plan exists for a 3D kernel after the 2D product is complete. Nothing from it ships yet, and nothing on this site claims otherwise.
site.content.timeline.threeD.title: Parametric 3D
site.content.workflow.annotate.body: Dimensions attach to geometry and follow it. Hatch regenerates when its boundary moves. Blocks carry attributes, so a plan can be counted into a schedule with a table instead of retyped.
site.content.workflow.annotate.title: Annotate so it survives edits
site.content.workflow.draft.body: Type L, C, TR or F and answer the same prompts. Fifteen object snaps, ortho and polar tracking and dynamic input next to the cursor keep the geometry exact. Grips, undo and the properties panel behave the way your hands expect.
site.content.workflow.draft.title: Draft with the commands you know
site.content.workflow.layout.body: Add a layout, set the paper, place viewports at 1:50 or 1:100, fill the title block. The same model can carry a general arrangement and a detail sheet without duplicating a line.
site.content.workflow.layout.prompt: _MVIEW Specify corner of viewport: scale 1:50 on A3 landscape
site.content.workflow.layout.title: Lay it out on paper
site.content.workflow.open.body: Drop a file on the dashboard or open it from the editor. Parsing runs in a Web Worker, so a large survey never blocks the UI, and the drawing renders as AutoCAD renders it: dimension values, text, fonts and lineweights included.
site.content.workflow.open.title: Open a DXF, or start blank
site.content.workflow.share.body: Plot to PDF with real lineweights, export SVG or an image, or write the DXF back out with its own layers, blocks and linetypes. Save keeps a version; a share link lets a reviewer open it in their browser too.
site.content.workflow.share.prompt: Saved v14 · exported GA-01.pdf · link copied
site.content.workflow.share.title: Plot, export, share
site.features.caps.blocks.alt: One door block definition placed three times along a wall
site.features.caps.blocks.body: Draw a door once, then place it forty times. Every instance points back at one definition, so correcting the original corrects the drawing — and attributes let each instance carry its own tag, which is what turns a plan into a schedule.
site.features.caps.blocks.title: Blocks and attributes
site.features.caps.dimensions.alt: A rectangle being stretched, with its dimension updating from 2200 millimetres
site.features.caps.dimensions.body: A dimension is attached to the geometry, not typed next to it. Stretch the wall and the measurement updates itself — which is the difference between a drawing you can trust and a drawing you have to re-check. Fifteen object snaps, dimension styles, hatch and tables come with it.
site.features.caps.dimensions.title: Associative dimensions
site.features.caps.dxf.alt: A DXF file opening in the editor and exporting back out to DXF
site.features.caps.dxf.body: Open a file from your desk, edit it, write it back out. Layers, blocks, dimension styles and text all survive the trip, so {{appName}} slots into a toolchain that already runs on DXF instead of asking everyone to move.
site.features.caps.dxf.title: DXF round-trip
site.features.caps.layouts.alt: A paper-space sheet with two viewports and a titleblock
site.features.caps.layouts.body: Model space is where you draw; paper space is where you decide what gets printed. Place viewports at a real scale, fill in the titleblock, and plot the sheet to PDF or SVG — the same drawing can carry a detail sheet and a general arrangement without duplicating any geometry.
site.features.caps.layouts.title: Layouts and viewports
site.features.caps.lede: Scroll and each one draws itself, in the order you would draft it.
site.features.caps.title: Four things a drafting tool has to get right.
site.features.closing.sub: The editor is free to use and DXF export is not behind a paywall. Sign up, drop a file, start typing commands.
site.features.closing.title: Open a drawing and try every one of these.
site.features.commands.lede: Type the alias at the command line or click the tool; the prompts that follow are the ones AutoCAD users expect, in fourteen languages.
site.features.commands.title: Every group, every command, its alias.
site.features.compare.caption: CADO compared with installed desktop CAD
site.features.compare.lede: Where CADO is ahead, where it is level, and where it is honestly not there yet.
site.features.compare.title: A browser tab against an installed seat.
site.features.details.dimstyles.body: A dimension is attached to the geometry it measures; stretch the wall and the value updates. DXF dimension styles import with their arrowheads, text height and precision, and per-dimension overrides in XDATA (including the plot-scale factor DIMLFAC) are honoured, so an imported drawing shows the values AutoCAD shows.
site.features.details.dimstyles.title: Are dimensions really associative, and do dimension styles survive import?
site.features.details.languages.body: Fourteen: the same set AutoCAD ships, command prompts included. English, Čeština, Deutsch, Español, Français, Magyar, Italiano, 日本語, 한국어, Polski, Português (Brasil), Русский, 简体中文 and 繁體中文. Translations other than English are drafted from established AutoCAD terminology and not yet professionally reviewed.
site.features.details.languages.title: Which languages does the interface speak?
site.features.details.layouts.body: Yes. Each layout tab has its own page setup (paper, orientation, margins, scale, plot style) and any number of viewports at their own scales. Viewports defined in an imported DXF are adopted and written back on export.
site.features.details.layouts.title: Can I have more than one layout, each with its own paper?
site.features.details.lineweights.body: Yes. Entities carry ACI colours and true lineweights, lineweights are honoured on screen and in the PDF, and a drawing whose default colour is white on a dark theme plots black on the white sheet, the same swap AutoCAD makes. Plot styles offer colour, monochrome and grayscale.
site.features.details.lineweights.title: Do lineweights and colours plot the way AutoCAD plots them?
site.features.details.offline.body: Drafting never needed the network: parsing, rendering, snapping and plotting all run in the tab. A save made offline is kept in the browser flagged for sync and sent when the connection returns; a recovery snapshot protects against a closed tab.
site.features.details.offline.title: What if my connection drops mid-drawing?
site.features.details.text.body: Single-line text and MText import with their styles; fonts are resolved per style, control codes and encodings are decoded, and MText is edited in place with an on-canvas editor. Find and replace works across text, attributes and table cells.
site.features.details.text.title: What happens to text, fonts and MText formatting?
site.features.details.themes.body: Twelve themes, eight dark and four light, recolour the chrome, canvas, grid and accents together. Monokai is the default; the choice follows your account across devices.
site.features.details.themes.title: Can I work on a light canvas?
site.features.details.three-d.body: Not yet. CADO is a 2D drafting editor. A phased plan for parametric 3D exists for after the 2D product is complete; nothing from it ships today.
site.features.details.three-d.title: Is there 3D?
site.features.details.title: The things drafters ask before they trust a tool.
site.features.formats.caption: File formats CADO reads and writes
site.features.formats.lede: DXF is the native exchange format and it is on every plan. Everything below is checked against AutoCAD, not against a spec sheet.
site.features.formats.title: What goes in, what comes out.
site.features.hero.lede: {{appName}} is not a viewer with a pencil bolted on. It is a full drafting editor: the command set, the snaps, the layouts, the DXF fidelity and the file management, with an assistant on top. This page lists what is there, group by group, with the alias you would type.
site.features.hero.title: Everything a 2D drafting tool has to get right, and the browser gets out of the way.
site.features.snaps.glyphs: Snap markers use the AutoCAD glyphs, so the square, triangle and circle mean what they have always meant.
site.features.snaps.lede: Every point you pick can lock to geometry that already exists. Ortho and polar tracking, a snap grid and dynamic input next to the cursor come with it, and all of them toggle from the status bar.
site.features.snaps.title: Fifteen object snaps, plus tracking.
site.home.ai.chatAlt: Example: the request 'change all red lines on layer DIM to blue' becomes a reviewed three-step plan
site.home.ai.example.prompt: change all red lines on layer DIM to blue
site.home.ai.example.recolour.label: Change colour
site.home.ai.example.risk.label: Risk
site.home.ai.example.select.label: Select entities
site.home.ai.lede: The assistant turns plain English into ordinary editor commands, then validates them before anything touches the drawing. It runs against a model you choose: a local Ollama server that never sees the network, or an OpenRouter key.
site.home.ai.point1Body: Colour words are filters, "on layer X" is a scope, "selected" is the current selection. An ambiguous request asks instead of guessing.
site.home.ai.point2Body: Every plan is labelled safe, review or destructive; destructive ones need a confirmation.
site.home.ai.point3Body: Actions land on the same undo stack as your own edits, and the audit log lives in your browser, not on our servers.
site.home.ai.title: Say what you mean. Review what it will do. Undo if you change your mind.
site.home.ai.undoWith: Applied plans can be undone with {{shortcut}}.
site.home.closing.sub: No install, no licence server, no conversion step. Sign up, drop a DXF on the dashboard, and it is on your screen as it was drawn.
site.home.cloud.caption: Every save is a version. Two people saving at once get a choice, not a silent overwrite.
site.home.cloud.conflicts.body: A save against a stale version is refused with Overwrite, Save as copy or Reload.
site.home.cloud.conflicts.title: Conflict detection
site.home.cloud.folders.body: A file manager for drawings: My Drawings with folders, Recent, Shared with me, Trash.
site.home.cloud.folders.title: Folders, trash, search
site.home.cloud.lede: Drawings save to your account with Ctrl+S, and every 30 seconds unsaved work is snapshotted in the browser in case the tab dies. Offline, the save is kept locally and goes through the next time you press Save with a connection.
site.home.cloud.orgs.body: Owner, admin, member and viewer roles; shared folders; view or edit links you can email.
site.home.cloud.orgs.title: Organizations
site.home.cloud.railAlt: A version rail: saves 12, 13 and 14, with a conflict at save 14 offering Overwrite, Save as copy or Reload
site.home.cloud.title: Never lose a line. Never lose an argument about which file is current.
site.home.cloud.versions.body: Every save is kept and can be restored from the dashboard.
site.home.cloud.versions.title: Version history
site.home.explorer.lede: Pick a group. Each command is listed with the alias you would type, next to a real screenshot of where it lives. Nothing here is a mock-up.
site.home.explorer.title: Seventy-odd commands, and the aliases your fingers remember.
site.home.facts.label: By the numbers
site.home.hero.lede: {{appName}} is a full 2D CAD editor that runs in the browser. Open a DXF exactly as AutoCAD drew it, draft with the same commands and snaps, lay it out on paper, plot to PDF and write the DXF back out. Your drawings are versioned in your account and shareable with a link.
site.home.hero.legendLabel: What a drawing is made of
site.home.hero.scrollHint: Scroll to pull the drawing apart
site.home.hero.title: The drafting tool you already know, in the tab you already have open.
site.home.pricing.compareAll: Compare every plan line by line
site.home.pricing.lede: Prices shown per user per month, billed annually. The full toolset and DXF export are on every plan, including Free.
site.home.pricing.title: Free for occasional drawings. Paid when it earns its keep.
site.home.sheet.lede: Move your pointer over the sheet and the coordinates track it in millimetres. Scroll, and the plan drafts itself in the order you would draw it: walls, openings, dimensions, hatch.
site.home.sheet.planAlt: Floor plan of a three-room apartment, 7000 by 3400 millimetres, with dimension lines and object snaps
site.home.sheet.title: It behaves like the CAD you learned on.

site.home.stack.fallbackAlt: A floor plan exploded into its layers, with a paper-space sheet on top

site.product.arch.footBefore: Sign-in is handled by Supabase Auth; the AI assistant talks to the model you configure directly from the browser. Read the
site.product.arch.lede: Parsing, rendering, snapping, hatching and plotting are all client-side. The API exists for identity, file management and durability, so a large drawing never needs a large upload to draw a line.
site.product.arch.storage.title: The drawings themselves
site.product.arch.title: The drafting happens on your machine. The server keeps the files.
site.product.closing.sub: Create an account, drop a DXF on the dashboard, and compare it with the original. That comparison is the product.
site.product.closing.title: See it with your own drawing.
site.product.fidelity.dims.body: Per-dimension overrides in XDATA, including the plot-scale factor DIMLFAC, are read, so a span reads 10280 where AutoCAD says 10280, not the raw 68.53.
site.product.fidelity.dims.title: Dimension values
site.product.fidelity.large.body: Parsing runs in a Web Worker; a 36 MB general arrangement opens without freezing the tab.
site.product.fidelity.large.title: Large files
site.product.fidelity.layouts.body: Viewports defined in the DXF are adopted with their camera and written back, so a sheet set survives the round trip.
site.product.fidelity.layouts.title: Layouts and viewports
site.product.fidelity.lede: The importer is checked against AutoCAD on real issued drawings, not against a spec sheet. These are the things that used to go wrong and no longer do.
site.product.fidelity.linetypes.body: The drawing’s own LTYPE table and $LTSCALE are written on export, so dashed centrelines come back dashed.
site.product.fidelity.linetypes.title: Linetypes
site.product.fidelity.lineweights.body: True lineweights on screen and on paper; ACI colours; white-on-dark defaults become black on the white sheet when plotting.
site.product.fidelity.lineweights.title: Lineweights and colours
site.product.fidelity.shotAlt: Detail of the imported drawing: half top plan and half bottom plan of a slab with dimension strings, weep holes and the title block.
site.product.fidelity.shotCaption: An issued general arrangement, as imported. No cleanup was done for this screenshot.
site.product.fidelity.text.body: Control codes and encodings are decoded; each text style resolves to its own font. Notes read as written.
site.product.fidelity.text.title: Text and fonts
site.product.fidelity.title: If AutoCAD shows it one way and CADO another, that is our bug.
site.product.hero.lede: This is a tour of the editor: what each part of the screen does, how model space and paper space relate, what runs in your browser and what runs on ours, and what actually happens when you press Save.
site.product.hero.title: One drawing. Two spaces. Nothing to install.
site.product.parts.canvas.detail: Three layers of canvas (grid, content, overlay) sized in device pixels, so lines are crisp on HiDPI screens. Middle-drag pans, wheel zooms about the cursor.
site.product.parts.canvas.label: The canvas
site.product.parts.cmd.detail: Type an alias or a full name; answer prompts with points, distances or options. Esc cancels, Enter repeats.
site.product.parts.cmd.label: Command line
site.product.parts.coords.detail: The cursor position in drawing units, or through the active viewport in paper space.
site.product.parts.coords.label: Coordinates
site.product.parts.docs.detail: Several drawings open at once, each with its own undo stack, layouts and unsaved marker.
site.product.parts.docs.label: Document tabs
site.product.parts.header.detail: Back, My Drawings (Ctrl+O), Save (Ctrl+S), Import a local DXF or image, Plot (Ctrl+P), and the light/dark switch.
site.product.parts.header.label: File actions
site.product.parts.rail.detail: Properties, Layers, Blocks, Views, Library, the AI Agent and Settings open as a drawer beside the canvas.
site.product.parts.rail.label: Panels rail
site.product.parts.ribbon.detail: Every tool also has a command alias. Drop-downs hold the variants: Circle 2P/3P/TTR, Arc methods, Trim/Extend, Fillet radius.
site.product.parts.ribbon.label: Draw, Annotate and Modify ribbons
site.product.parts.status.detail: OSNAP with its mode picker, SNAP & GRID, ORTHO, OTRACK, POLAR and DYN (dynamic input) toggle from here or with function keys.
site.product.parts.status.label: Drafting toggles
site.product.parts.tabs.detail: Model space is where you draw at full size. Each layout is a paper sheet with its own page setup and viewports.
site.product.parts.tabs.label: Model and layout tabs
site.product.parts.view.detail: Undo, redo, zoom extents, zoom in and out, viewport arrangement and the current layer.
site.product.parts.view.label: View controls
site.product.save.conflict.body: The condition fails, nothing is overwritten, and you are asked what to do: overwrite, save as a copy, or reload their version.
site.product.save.conflict.title: Someone else saved first
site.product.save.lede: Saving is concurrency-safe by construction. Two people can never write the same version, and the loser of a race is told, not overwritten.
site.product.save.offline.body: The save is kept in the browser flagged as pending and you are told so; press Save again once you are online and it goes through.
site.product.save.offline.title: No network
site.product.save.press.body: The editor serialises the drawing to DXF and sends it with the version it loaded.
site.product.save.press.title: You press Ctrl+S
site.product.save.reserve.body: A conditional update claims version 14 only if 13 is still current; then the payload is written to object storage under that version.
site.product.save.reserve.title: The API reserves the next version
site.product.save.snapshot.body: A recovery snapshot of unsaved work is written to the browser, so a closed tab or a crashed machine loses at most half a minute.
site.product.save.snapshot.title: Meanwhile, every 30 seconds
site.product.save.title: What Ctrl+S actually does.
site.product.spaces.lede: The same distinction AutoCAD makes, kept on purpose: geometry lives in the model, sheets frame it.
site.product.spaces.model.alt: Zoomed into the model: half elevation and half section of a bridge slab, with dimensions, notes and a schedule.
site.product.spaces.model.body: Everything is drawn in real units, one to one. Layers carry colour, lineweight and linetype; blocks carry attributes; dimensions measure the geometry they are attached to. This is the only place geometry lives, however many sheets end up printing it.
site.product.spaces.model.title: Model space: the drawing at full size
site.product.spaces.paper.alt: A layout tab: the white A-series sheet with a viewport showing the model, and the PSPACE indicator in the status bar.
site.product.spaces.paper.body: A layout is a sheet of a chosen size with viewports that frame regions of the model at a real scale, 1:50 on an A3 say. Title blocks, notes and the revision table are drawn on the sheet itself. Double-click into a viewport and every tool works through it (MSPACE); step out (PSPACE) and you are editing the sheet.
site.product.spaces.paper.title: Paper space: what gets printed
site.product.spaces.plot.alt: The Plot dialog: printer, paper size, plot area, scale, plot style and options, with a live preview of the sheet.
site.product.spaces.plot.body: Plot a window, the extents, the display or the layout to PDF with real lineweights, searchable text and embedded fonts, or to SVG, PNG or JPG. Publish writes every layout to one PDF. Export DXF writes the drawing back out with its own layers, blocks, linetypes and dimension styles.
site.product.spaces.plot.title: Plot: the sheet becomes a file
site.product.spaces.title: Draw once at full size. Print it as many ways as you need.
